qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507.mistake: The FOL statement p_6(Alessia ) → ¬enot p_7(Alessia )  represents a one-way implication: if Alessia appreciates history, then she does not  promote local traditions. However, the natural language statement is ambiguous, but does not clearly imply an exclusive or strict logical implication. More importantly, in the previous FOL statement and NL pair (p_6(Alessia ) → (p_7(Alessia )  ⊕ p_5(Alessia ))), it was stated that if Alessia appreciates history, then she can do exactly one of: promote local traditions or preserve cultural heritage. From that, p_6(Alessia )  implies either p_7 or p_5, not both. So, if she can  do p_7 (as an option), then p_6 does not imply ¬enot p_7 in general; rather, it implies mutual exclusivity with p_5, not p_7. Thus, the statement p_6(Alessia ) → ¬enot p_7(Alessia )  contradicts the earlier more nuanced constraint and is too strong. The natural language here says “she does not promote”, which may follow from the xor if other conditions hold, but the FOL here makes it unconditional upon p_5, which is incorrect. Thus, the mapping is invalid because it contradicts or oversimplifies the earlier logical structure. The FOL here wrongly eliminates the possibility of p_7 when p_6 is true unconditionally, while the earlier FOL allowed p_7 if p_5 is false. So this FOL is inconsistent with prior context. Hence, False.
